problem: Prior goal-oriented navigation surveys are organized by task (PointNav, ObjectNav, ImageNav, AudioNav) or by modality, so they miss the shared computational mechanisms across tasks and offer little cross-task comparison.
motivation: PointNav, ObjectNav, ImageNav and AudioGoalNav differ only in goal specification but share mechanisms for perception, representation and decision-making. A unifying view lets insights transfer across tasks and traces the shift from explicit geometric representations to implicit and generative ones.
key_idea: Organize about 200 goal-oriented navigation papers by six 'inference domains' (latent map, implicit representation, graph, linguistic, embedding, diffusion) across four goal modalities.
insight: The survey argues that the same inference domain adapts differently per task. Maps go from occupancy grids (PointNav) to semantic maps (ObjectNav), visual feature maps (ImageNav) and acoustic maps (AudioNav). Language matters more as semantic complexity grows, and audio and language representations are less developed than visual ones. These are qualitative observations with no ablation or quantitative evidence.
method: Inference-domain taxonomy: six domains (latent map, implicit representation, graph, linguistic, embedding-based CLIP/BLIP, diffusion) used to classify methods across tasks.

Task-wise review: separate sections for PointNav, ObjectNav (modular, end-to-end, zero-shot), ImageNav and AudioGoalNav, each with a summary table of year, venue, architecture type, datasets and metrics.

Preliminaries: unified formal definition (state, observation, action, goal spaces, policy), dataset/simulator comparison (HM3D, Gibson, MP3D, AI2-THOR, SoundSpaces, Habitat) and metrics (SR, SPL, SoftSPL, DTG, NE, PR, PPL, audio metrics).

Cross-task analysis: compares how each inference domain adapts across tasks (map content, implicit specialization, graph node semantics, language integration, embedding balance, diffusion for synthesis).
Challenges and future work: sim-to-real transfer, multimodal fusion, human-guided generalization, unified multimodal representation learning.
numbers_note: Survey paper; no experimental results, only tables listing methods, datasets and metric names.
results: No experiments. The survey reviews roughly 200 papers and proposes the six inference domains as a unifying taxonomy across PointNav, ObjectNav, ImageNav and AudioGoalNav. It concludes that combining map precision, language semantics and diffusion generation is promising.
limitations: No quantitative comparison of methods across benchmarks; tables list only datasets and metric names.

Coverage is uneven and the taxonomy is ad hoc, with some categorizations questionable. Instruction-following VLN is excluded, and the Discussion attributes NOMAD to ObjectNav although it is an ImageNav method.
Some content is duplicated: the audio table appears twice, and the section on ObjectNav modular methods overlaps with the domain descriptions.
